newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Say nothing, Spring counsels pre-budget Quinn.
newsitem.headline: Say nothing, Spring counsels pre-budget Quinn.

text.p: Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring has some advice for Finance Minister Ruari Quinn in the runup to next week's Irish budget - be inscrutable.

Spring, speaking at the opening of an Egyptian exhibit at the National Museum, said he could see that "leaders in Dynastic Egypt brought to a fine art the impenetrable facial expression which discloses nothing."
"These men might have resisted the most skilled and probing of journalists," said Spring, leader of the Labour party of which Quinn is also a member.
"I will be advising Ruairi Quinn to study closely and adopt that inscrutable expression in the days leading up to the budget," joked Spring, who is also Deputy Prime Minister.
Quinn is widely tipped to announce tax cuts next Wednesday in a pre-election budget. The cuts have had a huge buildup in the Irish press but Quinn has said nothing.
Spring said Government Buildings was not "an easy place to escape in the days prior to a budget" as the cabinet finalises its last budget before elections due by November.
He quoted a colleague who overheard two visitors to Government buildings speculating on the significance of the division bell which summons members of parliament to vote.
"What does that bell mean?" asked one.
"I don't know," said the other. "Maybe one of them has escaped."
